narrative.overview: DealBD feels like an established public desk where Bangladeshi shoppers compare evidence before acting. It is practical, accountable, information-rich, and easy to operate. Brand red works as a signal rather than decoration, while the decision lane aligns community confidence, deal evidence, and the next valid action.
keyCharacteristics: Compact, structured, and information-rich without becoming cramped.
One clearly dominant action per task region.
Borders, alignment, and restrained fills instead of routine shadows.
Familiar controls with direct, locally relevant language.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Brand red never substitutes for danger, and green never appears as decoration.

rules.name: The Borders Before Elevation Rule
rules.body: A surface earns elevation only when it actually moves above another interaction layer; ordinary page regions remain grounded.

dos: Do make price, title, merchant, status, and primary action readable first.
Do expose moderation, affiliation, expiry, and manually submitted price-history limitations.
Do use authored SVG icons or clear text labels.
Do give controls default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, error, and empty states.
Do explain what an empty state means and offer a valid next action.
donts: Don't use oversized promotional heroes inside the product.
Don't use gradients, glows, glass effects, or decorative motion.
Don't force every task into repeating same-size cards.
Don't give primary, secondary, destructive, and administrative actions equal emphasis.
Don't use Unicode glyphs as interface icons or decorative eyebrow labels above headings.
